newsitem.title: USA: Spiegel's losses double as catalog sales falter.
newsitem.headline: Spiegel's losses double as catalog sales falter.

text.p: Spiegel Inc. said Wednesday that its first-quarter losses more doubled to $31 million as sales through its famed catalogue fell by 9 percent, contributing to a 5 percent drop in overall revenues.

The company, whose retailing operations also include Eddie Bauer stores, said it recorded a net loss of $31.2 million, or 28 cents a share, in the three months ended March 29 compared with a loss of $14.3 million, or 13 cents a share, in the first quarter of 1996.
It added that total revenues slipped to $601.8 million from $634.7 million as it sold less merchandise through its mail-order operations, which account for 35 percent of total annual sales.
Spiegel said its disappointing catalogue sales resulted from lower customer response to its merchandise offerings and the impact on sales of the company's tightened credit policies.

The company, which is based in Downers Grove, Ill., said it was implementing new strategies aimed at repositioning its merchandise offerings and catalogue presentation to improve its results in that area.

"Spiegel Catalogue will continue to be challenged during this period of transition," President and Chief Executive John J. Shea said in a statement. "However, I am confident that the actions being taken will improve our performance."
Spiegel said sales at its Eddie Bauer subsidiary, which contributes 55 percent of total revenues, increased 4 percent for the quarter, based on sales at stores opened at least one year.
The company's stock lost 48.4 cents to $6.75 in afternoon trading on the Nasdaq market.
